newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to lift brothel ban, crack down on sex crime.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to lift brothel ban, crack down on sex crime.

text.p: Brothels will be legalised in the Netherlands so that local authorities can adopt better means of regulating prostitution, the Dutch government said on Tuesday.
"Prostitution is a fact of life...and this requires a realistic approach," Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager said in a letter to parliament.
The government should permit the exploitation of voluntary prostitution while cracking down on forms of prostitution involving coercion, abuse, violence or minors, she said.
Under existing legislation, prostitution is legal in the Netherlands, but brothels are not.
Sorgdrager argued that legalising brothel-keeping would enable local authorities to regulate the sector and improve prostitutes' working conditions.

"Local authorities can operate a system of permits whereby prostitution can shake off its associations with criminal activities such as drugs (dealing) and arms trading," the minister said in a statement.
At the same time, a bill put before parliament proposes tougher sentences on brothel keepers involved in forced prostitution or the exploitation of under-aged prostitutes.
The maximum penalty for these crimes will be raised from one to six years, while the bill will also make it easier to prosecute those who have sex with underage prostitutes.

Currently such cases cannot be prosecuted without a complaint having been brought. Waiving the complaint requirement would make it easier to prosecute cases of sex tourism and child prostitution, Sorgdrager said.
According to justice ministry estimates, there are around 30,000 prostitutes currently working behind the country's notorious 'red light' windows, in brothels, escort agencies and on the street.
Of these, around 40 percent are illegal immigrants from outside the European Union, some of whom are working against their will.

The proposed legislation aims to make it easier for police to crack down on trafficking in women. Brothels will be banned from employing illegal immigrants or prostitutes without a valid resident's permit.

To qualify for a licence, brothel-keepers will also have to comply with minimum hygiene, building safety and city planning standards, although the precise requirements will vary according to local ordinances.

Several major Dutch cities including Amsterdam have anticipated the draft legislation now before parliament and already operate permit schemes whereby they turn a blind eye to brothels which comply with certain stipulations.
